science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,280 K and log g 4.61 (u1 0.579, u2 0.179): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 2
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 17 days, fitted with starry to the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 2 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.88%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.70%, the light's own noise being 0.05%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43) list the star as a rotator in their table (VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2): a rotation period of 17.03 ± 1.41 d in campaign 2, with a periodogram peak of 0.34. The rotation and its period are theirs, taken as published; no criteria were applied to them here. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 2 other stars within 16 arcseconds, with 0.12% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 2

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffe9da, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 2 (August to November 2014): the map's scale, 97.5% to 102.5% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 4.7% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · August to November 2014
